questions.question: What is another name for the service line?
questions.explanation: The trailer service air line is also called the control line or signal line.

questions.question: Keeping cargo low can:
questions.explanation: A vehicle can roll over when turned too quickly. Keep cargo low and close to the ground. This lowers the center of gravity and helps prevent rollovers.

questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak
A valve that prevents the truck from being stolen
A valve that prevents the driver from going too fast
A valve that prevents the trailer from accidentally being released

questions.correctAnswerText: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve keeps air in the truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak.

questions.question: Trailers with low underneath clearance may be difficult to drive:
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are difficult to cross with a low-clearance trailer. Low-slung units and single-axle tractors pulling long trailers have special trouble crossing raised railroad crossings.

questions.question: The service air line is attached to the:
questions.explanation: The service air line carries air controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It is attached to relay valves, which apply the trailer brakes quickly.

questions.question: When lightly loaded, combination vehicles:

options.text: Should be loaded with most of the weight in the rear of the trailer.

questions.explanation: A lightly loaded vehicle has poor traction. The wheels lock up easily when braking. This reduces braking power.

questions.question: Test the tractor protection valve by:

options.text: Removing the parking brake control knob.
Releasing air with the brake pedal.
Releasing air with the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Releasing air with the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To test the tractor protection valve, let the air supply charge fully and turn off the engine. Press the brake pedal several times to release air. The valve should move to emergency position when pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: In a sudden turn, the ____ trailer is most likely to turn over.
questions.explanation: Turn slowly and smoothly. A quick turn while pulling trailers can cause the last trailer to roll over.

questions.question: To control surge when stopping, you should not:

options.text: Keep a steady pressure on the brakes.
Brake well in advance of a stop.

questions.explanation: To reduce surge in a tank vehicle, keep steady brake pressure and do not release the brakes too early. Brake well in advance and increase your following distance.

questions.question: When coupling, after you connect the air lines to the trailer, you should:
questions.explanation: Following the correct steps to couple trailers is important for safe operation. After connecting the air lines to the trailer, supply air to the trailer.

questions.question: Which type of vehicle is most likely to experience the "crack-the-whip" effect?
questions.explanation: Triple combinations are most likely to roll over due to the "crack-the-whip" effect.

questions.question: How should you load cargo to reduce rollover risk?

options.text: Load the cargo as far forward as possible.
Load the cargo as far back as possible.
Load the cargo as low as possible.
Stack the cargo as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Load the cargo as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Load cargo as close to the ground as possible. Also take curves and corners slowly to reduce rollover risk.

questions.question: Why do combination vehicles need more road space than other commercial vehicles?

options.text: Need more space to turn and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need more space to turn and stop.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are longer and need more space to turn and stop. Managing space properly is very important when operating these vehicles.

questions.question: What can happen if you change lanes too quickly in a combination vehicle?

options.text: A "crack-the-whip" effect that can cause a rollover.
Confusion over which lane the driver is using.
Other drivers to reduce their speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: A "crack-the-whip" effect that can cause a rollover.
questions.explanation: Changing lanes too quickly can cause a "crack-the-whip" effect that results in a rollover.

questions.question: Why should you not use the trailer hand valve while driving?

options.text: It will disconnect from the vehicle.
You will stop the vehicle too quickly.

questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve while driving. It can cause your trailer to skid.

questions.question: What happens when a trailer's wheels lock up?

options.text: The trailer tends to swing around.
The cab will swing, but the trailer will stay straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer tends to swing around.
questions.explanation: When a trailer's wheels lock up, it may swing out and hit other vehicles. This is especially likely with lightly-loaded trailers.

questions.question: What should you do to prevent a trailer from rolling over?

options.text: Speed up when nearing a corner.
Take on-ramps faster than the posted speed limit.

questions.explanation: To prevent rollover, keep cargo weight as low as possible and drive slowly around turns.

questions.question: What is the benefit of having anti-lock brakes on only one axle?

options.text: Will not make a difference in braking.
Will provide increased control in braking.
Will likely cause the air brakes to malfunction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will provide increased control in braking.
questions.explanation: Anti-lock brakes on even one axle give you more braking control than having no anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: What should you do if your trailer begins to skid?

options.text: Quickly turn the steering wheel one way, then the other.

questions.explanation: Release the brakes to help the wheels grip the road again. Once they grip, the trailer will straighten out and follow the tractor.

questions.question: Trailers made after what year must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS)?
questions.explanation: Trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
